sn12.68:1.1: Musīla is mentioned only here. | Saviṭṭha may also appear at [an3.21](), but it may be a different person, as that monk’s name is also spelled Samiddha, and the time, place, and people are all different. | Nārada appears in [an5.50](). | This monastery was favored by Ānanda, who was the teacher of Ghosita, the monastery’s donor ([sn35.129]()). He stayed there following the Buddha’s passing and the First Council ([sn22.90:4.2]()). It seems to me that many, perhaps all, of the discourses featuring Ānanda here were set in the period after the Buddha’s death, including this one.
sn12.68:14.3: See BB for notes on the reading. I don’t understand why BB translates “about” here. Normally the accusative is when you speak “to” someone, and as Narada is right there, why would it mean anything else?
